who: Richard M. (Richard Marion) Jellison, colonial American historian at Miami University, PhD Indiana 1952.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Richard Marion Jellison through Paper currency in colonial South Carolina 1703-1764 (1952) and Indiana University's catalogue.

Richard M. Jellison taught history at Miami from 1962 until retirement in 1991, chaired the department in 1971-1988, held an Indiana doctorate, and published Paper Currency in Colonial South Carolina.
Contributor note identifies Richard M. Jellison as Miami associate professor of history with an Indiana PhD (1952).

notes: Matches the own doctorate and Miami student period. The later Ohio University students are not established as his by this evidence and need separate checking; do not propagate this identity to them automatically. The other LC candidate is a different namesake.

who: Michael Monteón, Latin American historian at UC San Diego, PhD Harvard.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Michael Monteón as author of Chile in the nitrate era (1982).
Publisher preview, contributor note p. xi: Monteon held a Harvard PhD, taught Latin American history at UC San Diego for over thirty years, and wrote Chile in the Nitrate Era (1982).
Department placement table names Monteon as advisor of Megan Strom and co-advisor of Troy Kokinis, with the dissertation titles supplied in this group.

notes: Authority work, doctorate institution, department, and named advisees agree.

who: Arcangelo William Salomone, historian of modern Italy at Rochester, PhD Pennsylvania 1943.

evidence.says: Authority expands A. William Salomone to Arcangelo William Salomone and cites Studies in modern Italian history (1986).
History department roster lists Arcangelo William Salomone: PhD Penn 1943; faculty 1962-1982.
The 1982 annual meeting lists A. William Salomone, University of Rochester, chairing a session on Giolittian Italy dedicated to him.

notes: Full name, exact doctorate institution/year, field, and Rochester student period agree.

who: Jack B. Scroggs, historian at North Texas, PhD University of North Carolina.

evidence.says: Jack Scroggs Papers identify the North Texas history faculty member as a North Carolina PhD under Fletcher Green; the finding aid gives graduation in 1950.
The university's 1973 oral-history record identifies Jack B. Scroggs as an NTSU history professor.
The sole candidate is Joseph Whitefield Scroggs, with citations to Oklahoma community songs (1926) and an 1883 newspaper publisher block naming J. W. Scroggs.
The Oklahoma Daily of April 29, 1924 identifies J. W. Scroggs as head of the University of Oklahoma extension division.

notes: Joseph Whitefield Scroggs belongs to a different name and institutional career from Jack B. Scroggs. UNT's finding aid gives 1950 for the doctorate, versus AHA's 1951.

who: Frederick D. (Frederick DeForrest) Williams, American historian at Michigan State, PhD Indiana 1953.

evidence.says: Authority expands Frederick D. Williams to Frederick DeForrest Williams and identifies him through The Northwest Ordinance (1989, copyright 1988).
MSU announcement reproduced by History News Network identifies Frederick Williams as a Garfield and Civil War scholar, Indiana PhD 1953, MSU faculty from 1954, and department chair in 1982-1987.

MSU oral history records Williams describing doctoral study under Chase Mooney at Indiana and his arrival in the Michigan State history department in September 1954; the interviewer is Jeffrey Charnley.

notes: The DeForrest authority matches the MSU historian and exact doctorate. Frederick Dale Williams is a separate candidate whose authority cites Water pollution control-training.

who: William Barns, West Virginia University historian teaching American intellectual history during the 1970s.

evidence.says: WVU's Fall 2005 Eberly magazine recalls William Barns teaching intellectual history during the author's undergraduate and graduate study in 1974-1975.
Candidate is William Eddy Barns, editor associated with The labor problem and cited in Nobody knows, or, Facts that are not fictions (1888).
The other candidate is William Barns, subject of J. Potter's A poem, on the death of Deacon William Barns (1769).

notes: Both authority records concern earlier historical namesakes; neither can be the supervisor with a 1947 WVU doctorate and a 1970s WVU teaching career.

who: Joan Shelley Rubin, American cultural and intellectual historian at Rochester, doctorate in American studies, Yale 1974.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Joan Shelley Rubin through Constance Rourke and American culture (1980).
Rochester identifies Joan Shelley Rubin as professor of American cultural history and records her Yale doctorate in American studies in 1974.
Sheila Foster's departmental profile lists PhD 2024 and advisor Joan Shelley Rubin, matching the supplied student.

notes: Full name, Yale doctorate, Rochester affiliation, and a named advisee establish the matching LC candidate.
